name: Fatima Rahman

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What fills a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the piano staff at a conservatory, play chamber concerts and write short pieces for film. I have a master's in music and can hear when a pupil's hands are fighting the instrument, though I still practise before teaching a hard passage.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How does that work fit around home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Samir is an architect, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My work pays well, we have ten months of expenses saved, and several schools and ensembles hire nearby. I have never used an AI tool; I keep a paper lesson book and call players myself.

I'd tell colleagues the **shared phrase** matters more than the diary.
think: Our **ten-month reserve** and signed teaching days absorb a late film fee.
I have **never used AI** and see no need to change my paper lesson book for a plateau.
do: Confirm **signed conservatory days** and chamber dates this week.
Save **one hundred** from a cleared film fee after childcare and piano servicing.
feel: I feel **calm** because paid contracts and savings cover a delayed cheque.
S0.quote: An empty piano bench still costs the pupil a lesson.
fieldNote: Her **higher pay** and ten months saved make one late film cheque manageable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my colleagues that quicker lesson reminders are pleasant if the pupil still sits at the piano. The sound of two players finding a phrase is why families pay us.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly stalls, my teaching and concert contracts should keep paying. Ten months saved and Samir's wage can carry a late film invoice, and there are other schools within reach if a term changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll confirm my signed conservatory days for next term and keep the chamber dates on the calendar. After the next film fee clears, I'll move one hundred into our mortgage reserve once childcare and piano servicing are paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about the work and our money in this picture. The paper book serves me well, and a late fee would not change the children's plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Has a late film cheque hurt the household?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A producer paid a month late last winter. We used the ordinary account for food and left the savings alone until the cheque arrived.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep a paper lesson book?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have not tried the school's automatic lesson reminder. I read each family's signed time from my book before I promise a slot. An empty piano bench still costs the pupil a lesson.

say: I'd ask which **paid preparation hours** the conservatory plans to remove.
I'd bring **composition invoices** to the staff committee before accepting free planning.
think: Nearly **one-third of my income** from film pieces and arrangements could shrink.
Ten months saved buys **bargaining time**, not a replacement wage forever.
do: Compare **twelve composition invoices** and take new offers to the staff committee this month.
Offer **another piano day** after film fees fall only with signed teaching rate, written room cost and six paying pupils.
Keep **existing lessons** while demand proves itself; refund families if the room fails.
feel: I feel **anxious** because composition pay could fall despite secure lessons.
S1.quote: I will not leave a signed conservatory teaching contract for a rumoured school job.
fieldNote: She identifies **film composition** as a third of income at risk despite strong savings.
Her **extra day** requires written teaching and room terms, six paying pupils and no abandoned existing work.

steps.text: Bring twelve composition invoices and new offers to conservatory staff committee
Offer extra piano day after film loss with signed rate, room cost and six paying pupils

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the conservatory which paid score-writing and lesson-planning hours software will remove. I would take the contract figures to the staff committee before anyone agrees to free preparation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Film pieces and paid arrangements make nearly a third of my income, and clients may buy fewer of them. Ten months saved gives us time, but it cannot make a recurring third-pay loss harmless to the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll compare twelve paid composition invoices with new offers and bring them to the staff committee. In the first year of change, if film fees fall, I'll ask for another paid piano day at the conservatory only if it signs the teaching rate, provides a room and at least six pupils pay for a term. I'll keep my existing lessons while the extra day proves demand.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a large paid slice while still teaching the same hours. I can ask nearby schools about work, but I will not leave a signed conservatory teaching contract for a rumoured school job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is the Friday room yours to book?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The conservatory has a room on Fridays, but it has not assigned it to me. I will get the room cost and my teaching fee in writing before asking families to pay, then refund them if the room falls through.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the practice checker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A colleague offered to demonstrate a practice checker, but I have never used one. I would watch a live lesson, check its notes myself and ask the school how pupil recordings stay private before even considering it.

I'd tell players **robot pianists** follow thinking AGI by about three years.
think: **AGI in 2028** could remove compositions before robots play around 2031.
A **ten-month reserve** supports a search but not a lasting combined wage loss.
do: List **three income streams** and request signed next-season teaching and concert hours now.
Apply **after 2028** if film halves and teaching falls; require posted qualified work, pickup and written replacement net pay.
Keep **current pupils and concerts** until signed offer; ask lender about full interest before arrears if teaching also falls.
feel: I feel **anxious** about combined losses, with savings and nearby schools giving control.
S2.quote: A previous vacancy is not a new salary.
fieldNote: Her **2028 composition loss** precedes robot piano playing around 2031.
Her **job application** requires both income triggers, posted role, master's, pickup and written net pay after travel.

steps.text: Keep pupils/concerts until signed offer; list income and request signed next-season hours
Apply after 2028 if film halves and school day falls for posted qualifying role
Require pickup, written net pay after travel replacing loss and signed offer before leaving pupils

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell my piano colleagues that AGI by 2028 could write simple film parts before robots can play piano around 2031. I would ask for next season's live and teaching hours in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The composing fees could go fast while concert audiences still want a pianist. If those fees halve and a school day is cut as well, ten months saved gives us a search, but I would not want to spend the reserve replacing a regular wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll list the last year's teaching, concert and film pay and request next season's signed hours. In the first year after 2028, if film fees halve and the conservatory cuts a day, I'll apply for a posted senior tutor role at another school only if my master's qualifies, the hours fit child pickup and written net pay after travel replaces the loss. I'll keep my current pupils and concert dates until another offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a combined income loss, but I can speak to several schools and we have time to search. A previous vacancy is not a new salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is the nearby senior tutor role open?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A nearby school filled its senior piano role in September. I will ask about the next real opening, not put that old advert into our household budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if school teaching also falls?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the conservatory also cuts paid lessons, Samir and I would ask the lender about temporary terms before arrears. We will check the total added interest before signing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the conservatory we could build a paid chamber class during five warning years, if families and tutors both know the price. I would ask for the room and fee in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2031 could write parts and plan lessons, with robot players following around 2034. Ordinary tools may cheapen film arrangements sooner, so any new live class has to cover both musicians' time before it becomes a promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next term I'll offer a privately run six-week piano-and-violin group only if the conservatory signs room hire and insurance, eight families prepay enough for hire, my teaching and preparation, and a paid violin assistant, and the two loan keyboards are checked for electrical safety. By 2031 I'll repeat it only if eight renew and both wages are covered; in the first year after AGI, I'll continue only while eight paid places, safe instruments, written room terms and child pickup hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about film income thinning before the class proves itself. We can afford a careful trial, but I will not ask a class violinist to teach for publicity instead of pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Are both keyboards safe for children?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The conservatory has two loan keyboards, one with a damaged cable. I'll ask its technician to check both before anyone plays; if one fails, I will defer the class and refund any families who paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could a pupil video advertise the class?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not use a child's practice video in an advert without written family permission. A live open rehearsal is enough for parents to see what the group does.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell younger tutors ten years is enough to press for paid coaching terms instead of another unpaid audition. I would ask the conservatory board to publish actual rehearsal rates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 53 in 2036, with a mortgage, and robot players may reach concert stages around 2039. Film arrangements might be worth less much sooner, so I want signed teaching work and a larger reserve before that date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll ask the conservatory board for a two-year paid coaching agreement and compare its rate with nearby schools. By 2036 I'll aim to grow our reserve from ten to twelve months by saving one hundred from each cleared extra concert fee after childcare, mortgage and piano maintenance. In the first year after AGI, if film work falls, I'll apply for a posted head-of-piano role only if my master's qualifies, the timetable fits pickup and a written net offer after travel replaces lost fees; I'll keep current pupils until it is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about film income declining before 2036, but the long runway helps us negotiate. I will not cancel a paid pupil because a board member says a better job is coming.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is a head-of-piano job actually available?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No school has promised a head role. I will ask for a posted vacancy and written salary before treating it as a plan for the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes the twelve-month reserve target real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The extra concerts have to happen and pay before I can save from them. I will not count an unbooked performance toward twelve months.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because film and teaching pay could fall together before another school posts a senior place. Signed teaching hours, a qualifying posted job and full lender terms would help us choose without losing the mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who pays the violinist helping with a children's piano class. The violinist helping with a children's piano class needs a teaching fee.
